recentItems.title: The War on Terror 25 years on: Did it make us safer? | DW News
recentItems.description:
Al-Qaida's founder is long dead, but jihadist networks now stretch from Kabul to Lagos. Afghanistan fell back to the Taliban, and Iraq's and Syria's ISIS camps just emptied into chaos. DW traces 25 years of the War on Terror with an expert asking: "Did the world get safer — or did the threat just move? 
DW talks to: 
Hans-Jakob Schindler – Senior Director, Counter Extremism Project (CEP)
Stephanie Savell – Director, Costs of War Project
Amer Sabaileh – General Manager, Triageduepuntozero Think Tank
Agha-Nwi Fru – Executive Director, Sembe

recentItems.title: How Trump’s Gaza plans could strip Palestinians of their property rights | DW News
recentItems.description:
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has unveiled a plan that would see all of Gaza's population emigrating, following comments by Defense Minister Israel Katz that there was “no real solution for Gaza in the end without this migration” and that the government was “organized and prepared to get them [Palestinians in Gaza] out by sea, by air, by every way possible." Katz said explicitly that Israel was seeking support from US President Donald Trump for the mass emigration plan.  

Since January 2026, the US-led Board of Peace has reportedly been working on plans to rebuild the enclave from the ground up — albeit without announcing how exactly it will do that, and what becomes of Palestinians’ private property and their rights of ownership. Amid various leaks of the Board’s plans, the UN and multiple rights organizations repeatedly issued concerns of possible ethnic cleansing, which is illegal under international law.   

DW asked human rights experts about the legality of the plans — and spoke to landowners in Gaza, who say they simply want to stay on their land and have their right to self-determination respected.

recentItems.title: The United Nations votes to adopt a new map that shows Africa's true scale | DW News
recentItems.description:
The UN has adopted a resolution to adopt a new version of the world map that better represents the scale of the globe's continents. The old map was based on the so-called Mercator projection from 1569, which distorted the size of countries around the equator and in the polar regions. The 'correct the map' resolution was put forth by the African Union. 164 members of the UN voted in favor. Only the United States voted against.

recentItems.title: Lebanon’s border Christians: Life under Israeli military restrictions | DW News
recentItems.description:
Just a few kilometers from the Israeli border lies the Lebanese Christian town of Debel - inside what Israel calls a “yellow zone," an Israeli self-declared security zone which stretches from Israel's northern border some 10 kilometers into southern Lebanon. Other nearby towns, predominantly Shiite, have been evacuated and partially or entirely destroyed by the Israeli military. But Debel is one of three Christian towns in southern Lebanon where residents have maintained a presence. DW reporter Mohamad Chreyteh spoke with residents about life under Israeli military rule
